newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem slams Argentine violence, vows help for poor.
newsitem.headline: Menem slams Argentine violence, vows help for poor.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem said on Saturday that unemployment does not justify the protests which have swept many poorer parts of the country, but promised federal funds to create jobs.

"Unemployment cannot be converted into a matter of social agitation and discontent, nor into a matter for the courts with excesses and roadblocks and extremist attitudes," wrote Menem in an article carried by the state-controlled Telam news agency.
"This president, besides guaranteeing social justice, must fundamentally guarantee public order."
But Menem promised the creation of a "Promotion and Development Body" to create jobs and attempt to resolve the causes of the protests.

A wave of protest against poverty and unemployment started in April among teachers and oil workers in Patagonia and spread to the northern provinces of Salta and Jujuy and the central province of Cordoba.

Protesters in Jujuy were negotiating on Saturday with the government which had offered them a plan to create 10,000 new jobs if they lifted roadblocks. Over 100 people were hurt in clashes with police last week.

"The repeated episodes disturbing public order make it necessary to address the problems by creating a network of protection in critical areas," Menem wrote. "For this purpose we will spend 600 million pesos ($600 million) provided by the World Bank."
Menem added that the provincial governments will have to spend a dollar of their own money for each dollar of federal funding they receive under the plan to hit poverty.

The president promised not only money for the poor, but also harsh justice for violent demonstrators, whom he accused of "sheltering behind the weak while seeking the intervention of state security forces so that they can then shout out indignantly against 'indiscriminate repression.'"
Amnesty International said on Friday it had written to Menem expressing concern about "the apparent use of excessive force" by police and paramilitary police against demonstrators.
Menem laid the blame for the current 17.3 percent unemployment rate on old policies of previous governments which gave "artificial occupation to tens of thousands of people."
But Menem also said that inefficient provincial governments were partly responsible, despite what has said was a big rise in allocation of federal tax revenues to the provinces."
